texts: bad: two things go wrong at once. The parse asserts that families in general belong to the Keepers, which you never said, and it drops "Keeper" from the source restriction, widening the claim to apprentices from outside families of any kind; "the Keepers" also becomes a single named individual, which leaves "rarely" with no set of Keepers to be rare over. Rewrite as "Keepers rarely take apprentices from outside keeper families." — dropping "the" makes the subject the kind, so "rarely" has something to quantify, and the lowercase modifier fuses into an ordinary "keeper family" kind that keeps the restriction attached.

mixed: the permission itself is right, but the indefinite object is minted as a real apprentice and the acceptance is asserted, so the result claims the Council did accept an outside apprentice when the sentence only permits it; a false claim that an outside apprentice is a kind of "outside" is added too (our slip, not your wording). Rewrite as "The Council may accept outside apprentices." — a bare plural object stays at kind level, so no particular apprentice and no actual acceptance is asserted.

mixed: the change of kind is handled well, but "earlier" is dropped entirely — an attributive comparative with no stated standard has no licensed form — so the claim widens to "two outside apprentices became senior Keepers"; the per-member half is also missing, so if you later name one of the two, her own promotion is not derivable, and the same spurious "outside" claim appears here. Rewrite as "Two outside apprentices have already become senior Keepers." — "already" is a licensed marker that carries the "earlier" content the bare attributive cannot.
